fieldData.acrm---key-feature-4-content:
Insurance card photos read into fields

Patients photograph the front of their insurance card, and the app reads the member ID and group number into the intake. A field it cannot read clearly goes to the front desk.
fieldData.awb---key-feature-1-content:
The pain map Dr. Raleigh reads before 9:15

Larchmont Chiropractic sends the intake with each booking. Gideon Haas taps his lower back and right hip on the body chart and rates the back at 7 of 10. It started 3 weeks ago while moving a couch and gets worse after 30 minutes of sitting. Dr. Imogen Raleigh gets the answers on an email card before his 9:15 exam.
fieldData.awb---mockup-data: window.awbMockup = { newPatients: "I run Larchmont Chiropractic. Build a chiropractic intake form that goes out with every new booking. Ask patients to tap each spot that hurts on a front and back body chart, rate it from 0 to 10, say when it started and what they were doing, and pick what makes it worse. Email the chiropractor a card with the answers before the exam.", carAccidentCases: "Build an intake for Sorrel Ridge Chiropractic that asks whether a car accident caused the pain. On a yes, ask for the accident date, the auto insurer, the claim number, and the attorney, if there is one. Send those intakes by email to my case coordinator, Wendell Kim, instead of the health plan queue.", treatmentConsent: "My clinic is Bellmoor Chiropractic. Put our consent to care on the last screen of the intake and have patients sign it on their phone with a finger. Save the signature with the time it was signed, and show the front desk a list of today's first adjustments with whether each consent is signed.", reExams: "Build a re-exam form for Quarry Hill Chiropractic that sends the pain questions from the intake again at visit 12: the neck pain rating from 0 to 10 and how many minutes the patient can sit at a desk before it hurts. Show the chiropractor the intake answers and the visit 12 answers side by side." };
